run_findings.oauth_introspection_revocation_gate: RFC 7662 supports request-time token active/revoked checks at the authorization server. With no stale cache and fail-closed enforcement this is REVOCATION_AWARE_REQUEST_GATE; cached active=true can outlive revocation, so freshness must be represented explicitly.
run_findings.oauth_revocation_validation_path: RFC 7009 distinguishes self-contained access tokens from handle/reference tokens. Immediate revocation visibility depends on the resource-server validation path, not merely on token jti/signature/expiry.
run_findings.dpop_scope: RFC 9449 DPoP sender-constrains OAuth tokens and reduces replay, but the RFC says DPoP proof alone is not access control and the underlying token must remain valid. Classify PROOF_OF_POSSESSION_ONLY.
run_findings.biscuit_revocation_freshness: Biscuit exposes revocation identifiers and verifier-side list rejection, but its spec intentionally does not mandate revocation-ID publication/distribution. A locally checked stale list remains REVOCATION_STATE_FRESHNESS_UNPROVED.
run_findings.nonos_effect_side_epoch_gate: Current NON-OS/nonos-micro-kernel main c6f021d10278d1494d88835dd8c98b041ef13d65 signs process revocation_epoch into capability tokens, increments it before replacing authority on revoke, compares token epoch against current process epoch in the syscall resolver, and only constructs the handler Capability witness after resolver success. This is a concrete EFFECT_SIDE_REVOCATION_EPOCH_GATE, stronger than detached ALLOW replay but not a cross-system TRUE_EXTERNAL_REVISION_GATE.
run_findings.contextforge_fail_open_counterexample: Current IBM/mcp-context-forge main 555a9f3be253290151ac51ed45fbdca4565f132b documents JTI-backed token revocation for normal auth/MCP paths, but revocation/user DB lookup failures currently fail open for availability. Capability detection must capture outage semantics; classify REVOCATION_GATE_FAIL_OPEN for high-impact effect gating.
run_findings.classifier_self_test: AUTH_EFFECT_PROVENANCE_MATRIX_20260829_0520_V3.py was self-tested before persistence: 22 fixtures and 7 provenance invariants passed. It adds CAPABILITY_TOKEN, REVOCATION_ID, REVOCATION_EPOCH, PROOF_OF_POSSESSION, revocation freshness, fail-open/fail-closed, and effect-side epoch comparison evidence.
run_findings.true_external_revision_gate_bounded_nega: Across Authzed/SpiceDB, Permify, OpenFGA, OPA/Envoy, Cerbos, OAuth standards, Biscuit, Macaroons, ContextForge and NØNOS, no sampled cross-system external effect API accepted a prior independent authorization decision revision and atomically rejected it when stale. NØNOS supplies the strongest same-authority epoch analogue. This is a bounded negative only.
